bib.title: DeepSeek-Prover: Advancing Theorem Proving in LLMs through Large-Scale Synthetic Data

question: Can large-scale synthetic Lean 4 proof data, built by autoformalizing informal competition problems and iteratively self-training a prover, lift an LLM's whole-proof theorem proving?
hypothesis: Training on a large, quality-filtered synthetic corpus of formal statements with verified proofs, regenerated over iterations, makes the prover stronger and the data better.
contributions: An iterative method to synthesize 8 million formal statements, each with a formal proof, from informal math problems.
State-of-the-art whole-proof results on Lean 4 miniF2F and FIMO with a 7B model.
Open-sourcing a large dataset of formal proofs (and the model).

method.summary: Autoformalize 869,659 informal competition problems into Lean 4 statements with a fine-tuned DeepSeekMath-Base 7B, filter them by model scoring and hypothesis rejection (712,073 kept), prove statement and negation concurrently, verify with Lean 4, fine-tune on verified pairs and repeat. Final dataset is 8,066,621 verified statement-proof pairs.
method.task: Lean 4 whole-proof generation (automated theorem proving) with synthetic data via expert-iteration-style self-training

datasets.name: Scraped informal math problems
datasets.source: web scraping of high-school and undergraduate exercises, exams and competitions

datasets.name: Filtered formal statements
datasets.preprocessing: drop statements scored fair or poor; drop statements whose hypotheses prove False

datasets.name: Synthetic proof data
datasets.source: Lean-verified proofs of statements or their negations
datasets.preprocessing: Lean 4 verification; negated-statement proofs kept as augmentation

datasets.name: MMA
datasets.source: Jiang et al. 2023: Lean 4 mathlib formal statements back-translated to natural language by GPT-4
datasets.preprocessing: used to fine-tune the autoformalization ability

datasets.name: FIMO
datasets.source: Liu et al. 2023, IMO shortlist in Lean 4

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning on verified theorem-proof pairs (and on MMA for autoformalization); iterated until gains become marginal
training.tokens: 3.108B tokens for the autoformalized-statements ablation model (Table 2)

other.number_of_iterations: Table 4 reports iterations 0 to 4; number used for the final model is not stated
other.proof_search_k: each proof search stream attempts up to k proofs; k not stated

inference.samples: pass@1 (greedy), 64, 128, 8192, 65536 on miniF2F-test; 100 and 4096 attempts on FIMO
inference.prompting: autoformalization prompt: 'Mathematical Problem in Natural Language: {$informal_statement_with_answers} Translate the problem to Lean 4 (only the core declaration):'; scoring uses CoT with miniF2F-valid few-shot examples (count not stated)

parameters.quality_classes: excellent, good, above average, fair, poor; fair and poor removed
parameters.hypothesis_rejection: attempt to prove the statement with False as conclusion; success excludes the statement
parameters.negation_search: prove P and not-P concurrently, stop when either is proved
parameters.incorrect_statement_rate: at least 20% of filtered autoformalized statements were incorrect

other.verification_prefix: Lean 4 code prefix of Mathlib imports, set_option maxHeartbeats 0, open Nat Real Rat BigOperators (Appendix A.4)

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: at least one valid proof among the first k attempts, checked by Lean 4

metrics.name: cumulative
metrics.definition: proportion proved by any run/budget combined; not defined further

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds or confidence intervals. Ablations at pass@128.

availability.code: stated that code, model and data will be released; no URL
availability.data: synthetic dataset will be made available

prompts.text:
Mathematical Problem in Natural Language:
{$informal_statement_with_answers}
Translate the problem to Lean 4 (only the core declaration):
```lean4
Response:
{$formal_statement}
```

Five criteria (Relevance to Current Research, Complexity and Depth, Interdisciplinary Potential, Community Needs and Gaps, Innovativeness), then 'Customize your evaluation for each problem accordingly, assessing it as excellent, good, above average, fair or poor', answered as 'Translate the code to natural language / Analysis / Assessment'. Full text in Appendix A.1.

evidence.quote: global batch size of 512 and a constant learning rate of 1 × 10−4,

results.claim: DeepSeek-Prover reaches 46.3% on miniF2F-test with 64 samples, against GPT-4-turbo 0409 at 23.0%.
results.setup: Lean 4 miniF2F-test, whole-proof generation, DeepSeek-Prover 7B, 64 generations
results.note: Table 1 prints GPT-4 as 23.0%, section 4.2 text as 22.95%.

results.claim: Cumulative miniF2F-test success across budgets is 52.0% and 60.2% on valid.
results.setup: Lean 4 miniF2F-test, all runs combined; baseline is Hypertree Proof Search 600M
results.quote: cumulative scores of 60.2% on miniF2F-valid and 52.0% on miniF2F-test

results.claim: Scaling samples raises miniF2F-test pass rate from 30.0% greedy to 50.0% at 65536 samples.
FIMO: 4 of the problems proved with 100 attempts, 5 with 4096, GPT-4 none.
results.note: Problem count printed as 148 in abstract and intro, 149 in section 4.2.

results.claim: Training on 3.108B tokens of autoformalized data beats training on 0.238B tokens of mathlib at pass@128.
results.setup: DeepSeekMath-Base 7B trained with expert iteration on autoformalized vs mathlib data; untrained base is 27.5%
results.table: Table 2, row Autoformalized Statements, column miniF2F-test

results.claim: Training on high-score statements beats training on low-score ones by 4.5 points on test.
results.setup: equal amounts of high-score (excellent, good, above average) vs low-score (fair, poor) proof data
results.table: Table 3, row "excellent", "good" and "above average", column miniF2F-test
results.note: Text says 4.5%; test gap 42.6-38.1=4.5, valid gap is 7.4 (48.8 vs 41.4).

results.claim: Pass@128 on miniF2F-test rises monotonically over 5 iterations from 34.0% to 46.3%.
results.setup: iteration 0 vs iteration 4; valid goes 38.1% to 59.4%

results.claim: Scaling the synthetic data from 1,000 to 8,066,621 examples lifts pass@128 test from 24.18% to 40.16%.
results.setup: subsets of the 8M dataset; gain roughly proportional to exponential increase in size
results.note: Full-data row (42.62 valid, 40.16 test) differs from Table 2/3 autoformalized row (48.8, 42.6) at the same pass@128 without explanation.

results.claim: At least 20% of autoformalized statements are incorrect even after quality filtering.
results.quote: at least 20% of the formal statements generated by our model

limits: Authors concede the work focuses on algebra and number theory at middle-school and undergraduate level; broader diversity is future work.
Preprint, under review; code, model and data are promised, not linked.
No seeds, confidence intervals, optimizer, hardware, compute, sequence length, sampling temperature or number of final iterations reported.
Cumulative scores combine runs and are not comparable to fixed-budget pass@k.
Ablations are pass@128 only; inconsistent full-data numbers between Table 2/3 and Table 5.
Scoring-filter ablation fine-tunes with 'equal amounts' of data, without stating sizes.
Baselines differ in method (tree search vs whole-proof) and budget, so comparison is loose.
Supervised self-training on verified proofs (expert iteration) with a verifier as filter; no preference or RL loss is used despite the section mapping.

terms.definition: using the model to attempt proving the formal statement with 'False' as the conclusion; a successful proof indicates an invalid hypothesis, prompting exclusion
the scenario where at least one valid proof is discovered among the first k attempts generated by the model
